paragraphs.paragraph: Comfort, Renewal, and New Life in Jerusalem
paragraphs.title: Comfort, Renewal, and New Life in Jerusalem

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “I am returned unto Zion.”
easy.q: To whom does the LORD promise to return?

easy.explanation: Jerusalem shall be called “a city of truth.”
The streets shall be full of “boys and girls playing.”
easy.q: Who shall play in the streets of the city?

answers: That the city shall be a city of truth
That the city shall remain empty
That the city shall be far from the people
medium.explanation: The LORD will dwell in Jerusalem, and it shall be called a city of truth.
medium.q: What does the LORD’s presence in Jerusalem promise?

medium.explanation: The word describes something that seems astonishing or difficult to believe.
medium.q: What does “marvellous” mean in this passage?

answers: The LORD’s return, security, life, and the people’s return
The abandonment and destruction of Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The passage describes the LORD’s return, safe inhabitants, children at play, and the return of His people.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes the promised renewal?

answers: Their presence shows a city where people can live safely
They are preparing to leave Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: Old people and children openly living in the streets portray stable and secure life.
challenge.q: What do the old men and children in the streets show about the promised security?

answers: It is based only on power
It is established in truth and righteousness
challenge.explanation: The people shall be the LORD’s people, and He shall be their God in truth and righteousness.
challenge.q: What does “in truth and in righteousness” teach about the relationship between the LORD and His people?

answers: A renewal involving both gathering the people and restoring their relationship with God
challenge.explanation: The LORD promises to save His people, bring them to Jerusalem, and be their God.
challenge.q: What does the movement from the east and west countries to dwelling in Jerusalem emphasize?

paragraphs.idea: Comfort, Renewal, and New Life in Jerusalem

answers: Because the house of the LORD was being built
Because they were leaving the land
Because they were stopping their work
easy.explanation: They are urged to be strong as the foundation of the LORD’s house has been laid so the temple may be built.
easy.q: Why are the people told to let their hands be strong?

easy.explanation: The vine shall give fruit, the ground shall give increase, and the heavens shall give dew.
easy.q: What will the LORD give the land?

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “Let none of you imagine evil in your hearts against his neighbour.”
easy.q: What must a person not imagine in his heart against his neighbour?

answers: There was no hire and no peace because of affliction
medium.explanation: There was no hire for man or beast, and no peace for those who went out or came in.
medium.q: What was the condition before the new days?

medium.explanation: The passage says there was no hire, meaning no payment or wages for labor.
medium.q: What does “hire” mean in this passage?

answers: Blessing is joined with truth, judgment, and peace
Blessing removes all responsibility from the people
Blessing is meant only for rulers
medium.explanation: Along with promises of peace and increase, the LORD commands truth, judgment, and peace.
medium.q: How are blessing and social conduct connected in these verses?

answers: A move from hardship, insecurity, and conflict to blessing and peace
A move from abundance to poverty
A move from joy to fasting
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts former affliction and conflict with a future of prosperity and blessing.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the past and the promised present?

answers: Because truth is required in community life as well
challenge.explanation: The social commands show that the truth associated with Jerusalem must also govern the people’s conduct.
challenge.q: Why does the command to speak truth fit the description of Jerusalem as a city of truth?

answers: That the LORD will turn the people’s troubled condition into good
That the heathen will stop speaking
challenge.explanation: The LORD promises to save Judah and Israel so that they shall be a blessing.
challenge.q: What does the change from being a curse among the heathen to being a blessing teach?

paragraphs.paragraph: The Transformation of the Fasts into Days of Joy
paragraphs.title: The Transformation of the Fasts into Days of Joy

easy.explanation: The fasts shall become “joy and gladness, and cheerful feasts.”

answers: The fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth fasts
easy.explanation: The verse names the fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months.
The LORD commands, “Therefore love the truth and peace.”
easy.q: What are the people commanded to love?

answers: They will remain days of mourning only
They will become days of joy and cheerful feasts
medium.explanation: The fasts shall be transformed into joy, gladness, and cheerful feasts.
medium.q: What change is described concerning the fasts?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes happy and celebratory festival occasions.
medium.q: What does “cheerful feasts” mean in this verse?

medium.explanation: The verse concludes with the command to love truth and peace.
medium.q: What appears alongside the transformation of the fasts into joyful days?

answers: Public joy is joined with moral renewal
Joy has no connection to conduct
Truth and peace are forbidden during celebration
challenge.explanation: The change from fasting to joy is accompanied by a call to love truth and peace.
challenge.q: What does the connection between joy, truth, and peace teach?

answers: A painful past will be transformed into a time of joy
The people will stop remembering the past
The people will have no further relationship with God
challenge.explanation: The former fast days will become occasions of joy and celebration.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the change from fasts to cheerful feasts?

challenge.explanation: The verse directly commands the people to love truth and peace.
challenge.q: What explicit moral condition accompanies the promised change?

paragraphs.idea: The Transformation of the Fasts into Days of Joy

easy.explanation: People and the inhabitants of many cities will come to Jerusalem.
easy.q: Where will people from many nations come?

answers: To pray before the LORD and seek Him
easy.explanation: They will come to pray before the LORD and seek the LORD of hosts.

answers: The skirt of him that is a Jew
easy.explanation: Ten men shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew.
easy.q: What will ten men take hold of?

answers: From individuals and cities to many peoples and strong nations
From many nations to one person only
From Jerusalem to an unknown place
medium.explanation: The passage moves from inhabitants of cities inviting one another to the arrival of many peoples and strong nations.
medium.q: How does the movement described in these verses expand?

answers: To approach Him in worship and prayer
medium.explanation: The phrase appears with seeking the LORD and describes approaching Him in prayer.
medium.q: What does “to pray before the LORD” mean in this passage?

answers: They have heard that God is with him
medium.explanation: They say, “We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you.”
medium.q: Why will the nations ask to go with the Jew?

answers: They regard him as a person associated with God
They want to rule over him
They think he has no connection with God
challenge.explanation: Their desire to go with him is based on the report that God is with him.
challenge.q: What does the nations’ appeal to the Jew reveal about his standing?

answers: Jerusalem becomes a place where the nations seek the LORD
Jerusalem becomes a place the nations avoid
Jerusalem is described as having no significance
challenge.explanation: Many peoples and strong nations will come to Jerusalem to seek the LORD and pray before Him.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between Jerusalem and the coming of the nations?

answers: The invitation to seek the LORD includes many different peoples
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the wide variety of languages and nations involved.
challenge.q: What does “out of all languages of the nations” suggest?
